item.content:encoded:
Moveave and Kamea tribes in Gulf Province will sign a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) on the 14th of this month, November, to end their long-running tribal conflict at Upper Taure, Hinenga, Fish Creek in the Taure Lakekamu Local Level Government.

The date has been set by the Provincial Executive Council, while the venue has been selected to be at Urban Malalaua Local Level Government, Kerema District.

The tribes met for the fourth time on the 31st of October to negotiate the venue and date for the MOA to be signed between the two ethnic groups.

It was revealed that a ceasefire agreement already exists, however it will be amended to capture the current concerns and grievances of both parties before the signing.

President for Taure-Lakekamu LLG, Herbert Pokana, and relatives of those who lost lives during the conflict, asked both parties if they wanted genuine peace and if they were serious about putting the issue to rest once and for all.

Both parties, after sharing their grievances on how the conflict has affected their livelihoods, agreed that they wanted peace.

The conflict reportedly started in September 2024 and has since resulted in loss of lives and several people injured. The ongoing conflict has limited access to basic government services for both communities and disturbed peace within Kerema district.

For the peace process, K300,000 will go to the affected families — K100,000 for each of the three families affected, and K200,000 will be shared between the two tribal groups — K100,000 each to make peace the Melanesian way with food and pigs.

Attending the meeting were community leaders, peace committee members and ward councillors from both parties, the Acting Police Station Commander – Inspector Pius Koma, and the President for Taure-Lakekamu LLG, President Herbert Pokana.

item.title: El Nino take toll on communities in Northern
item.description: El Niño has taken a toll on many communities and villages throughout the country, and Northern Province is no exception. The prolonged drought has left people without water, food and severe health issues.
item.content:encoded:
El Niño has taken a toll on many communities and villages throughout the country, and Northern Province is no exception.

The prolonged drought has left people without water, food and severe health issues.

With the National Government's initiative to address the El Niño issue in the country, a funding of 300 million Kina has been sourced from the World Bank to assist the people of PNG in these trying times.

The National Government made a decision on the borrowed funds where each provincial governor will receive K10 million while the districts will receive K5 million.

However, K2.5 million each has been released to the districts and provincial governments to conduct the first phase of the El Niño relief program.

While in Northern province, the three districts have received K2.5 million each together with the Oro Provincial Government (OPG).

The three districts of Northern province, namely Sohe, Ijivitari and Popondetta, have formulated their relief contingency plans to facilitate relief assistance to their respective districts.

Meanwhile, the OPG's K2.5 million has been strictly put aside for water supply projects in severely affected communities.

item.title: Biru CS opens new staff house
item.description: The Biru Correctional Service (CS) Institute in Oro Province opened a new staff house recently, marking a milestone achievement for the institution. Outgoing Commanding Officer, Chief Inspector Samuel Kiap, said funds for the staff house opening came from the institution's own internal projects such as poultry, cocoa and oil palm.
item.content:encoded:
The Biru Correctional Service (CS) Institute in Oro Province opened a new staff house recently, marking a milestone achievement for the institution.

Outgoing Commanding Officer, Chief Inspector Samuel Kiap, said funds for the staff house opening came from the institution's own internal projects such as poultry, cocoa and oil palm.

Mr Kiap said this achievement has come a long way with dedicated officers who worked closely under the management to achieve such a project in the institution.

He highlighted the importance of self-reliance, saying Biru is one institution that has succeeded from its own projects and has brought changes to the institution going forward.

Kiap said under his leadership, the staff house project cost the institution K60,000.

He said such good infrastructures are in place to boost the existing facility at the institution, and the asset must be kept in a good condition.

On this note, Kiap urged the Biru CS officials to work in unity and see progress at the Biru CS institution.

"We are out of support from the authorities, we at Biru can make a difference with the little we have," he said.

Mr Kiap has been in the position of Jail Commander for two and a half years and he will be leaving the institution to Acting Caretaker Commander, Senior Inspector Ludwick Monduk, while he travels for further studies overseas.

Kiap, under his leadership, also initiated and delivered single men's barracks housing 10 officials, built an institutional clinic, a staff house, cocoa fermenter and increased the poultry project.

item.content:encoded:
​For years, the sound of gunfire across Hela Province carried a single message: destruction. But on Saturday, November 7, a silent quiet fell over Komo Station—punctuated not by bullets, but by the thud of 120 factory-made rifles and more than 1,000 homemade firearms hitting the ground.

​In a province where tribal conflict has long cast a shadow over future generations, the mass surrender marks one of the most significant breakthroughs yet for Hela’s ongoing Gun Surrender and Amnesty Programme.

​Behind the staggering pile of surrendered iron lay months of exhausting, behind-the-scenes diplomacy. Community elders, traditional authorities, and provincial leaders spent sleepless nights negotiating with warring tribes, appealing to a shared desire to break the cycle of violence.

The programme was led by the Governor of Hela Province, Philip Undialu, alongside Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu, Komo Hulia MP Daniel Tindipu, Provincial Election Manager John Tipa and other prominent provincial leaders.

Mr Angu says the people of Komo have sent a powerful message to the rest of Hela Province: the time has come to put down the guns, embrace peace and build a better future for the next generation.

"Our children did not create these conflicts, nor did they create the gun culture that has caused so much suffering in our communities. Yet they are the ones growing up with the consequences of our decisions.

"It is our responsibility as parents, leaders and communities to change that story.

"We must ask ourselves one important question: What kind of future do we want our children to inherit? Do we want them to inherit guns, tribal conflicts, fear and destruction, or do we want them to inherit peace, education, opportunities and a prosperous society?

"Today, we must make a choice. We either continue investing in destruction, or we begin investing in peace, security and development. Hela cannot afford to sacrifice another generation to tribal fighting," Angu said.

He said the continuous loss of young lives, destruction of properties and disruption of essential services must come to an end.

"We cannot continue burying our young men, destroying our properties and denying our children opportunities because of conflicts that can be resolved through dialogue, reconciliation and responsible traditional leadership.

"Every bullet surrendered is a life potentially saved. Every gun removed from our communities is another opportunity for a child to grow up without fear," he said.

item.title: New vehicles and boats to strengthen family health services in Madang
item.description: The Madang Provincial Health Authority (MaPHA) has purchased nine new vehicles and six new boats, at a cost of more than K2 million, in a bid to strengthen outreach and patrol programs to the rural communities, particularly family health services. The ten- seater vehicles and boats were officially handed over to the six districts last Friday by MAPHA's Chairman, Dr Boga Figa.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Provincial Health Authority (MaPHA) has purchased nine new vehicles and six new boats, at a cost of more than K2 million, in a bid to strengthen outreach and patrol programs to the rural communities, particularly family health services.

The ten- seater vehicles and boats were officially handed over to the six districts last Friday by MAPHA's Chairman, Dr Boga Figa.

The boats will complement the vehicles to reach coastal, island, and river communities where there is no road accessibility.

The other two vehicles will be used by officers at the provincial headquarters, whilst the dyna truck will be used for delivery of medical drugs to the districts.

The decision to buy the vehicles and boats was made by the MaPHA Board last year.

Dr Figa urged proper use of the vehicles and the boats, stating they are not to be used as ambulance or for shopping.

He also thanked all partners of Madang PHA the six district MPs, and the Madang Provincial Executive Council for their ongoing support, which made it possible for Madang PHA to keep delivering services in times of extreme difficulties.

Dr. Figa said all their support have improved Madang's health indicators.

"Our report for Madang since this Board was installed in 2024 was right at the bottom of the ladder. Of the 22 provinces, we were ranked last. We were like the rug that other provinces stepped on to clean their feet. However, from 2025 to 2026, there's been a tremendous improvement in our performance. We are now ranked number 10. Madang is now the 10th best performing PHA in the country.

"We can still improve on that. We can reach the single figure digit. We did it without these ones, the vehicles, and boats. Our challenge now is to use these enabling fleets to further improve our service delivery to the people of Madang Province," Dr Figa said.

The Chairman also made special mention of Middle Ramu and Raikos districts, whose performances have been outstanding; contributing to Madang's improvement in the national ranking.

"To those districts on the whiteline, you should have no more excuses whatsoever not to deliver MCH clinics and other programs. You now have vehicles and boats. Maternal and Child Health care contributes significantly to our ranking," he said.

Dr. Figa further emphasized that despite critics, the decisions they are making are to serve the children in rural districts.

He said, "Some decisions we make will not be very popular. But we are not in a popularity contest for the Miss or Mr PNG. We are not here to please everyone. We are doing this for the sake of our children in the big bush.

"Whatever little funds we have, we are carefully managing to serve our people."

MaPHA's Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Martin Daimen, reiterated the Chairman's remarks, saying MaPHA is directly equipping the Public Health Directorate and Family Health Services teams to extend the patrols and outreach programs, deliver immunisations, support maternal and child health, and ensure that health services reach the rural areas, river communities and maritime populations.

Giving a situational analysis of MaPHA's performance in the last few years, Dr. Daimen stated that Madang Province has been consistently at the bottom of the table, even before the launching of the PHA reform.

"Immunisation and Ante Natal coverage were both less than 50 %.

"All rural health facilities did not have program vehicles for more than 10 years. Vehicle hires consumed 60% of our budget during immunisation program implementation, and our manpower was reduced to below 50%, Dr. Daimen revealed.

He pointed out that the most critical essentials and enablers of health services delivery are a skilled workforce, adequate finances, and reliable, effective, and efficient transportation system.

The CEO reiterated that the decision to purchase the vehicles and outboard motors was reached last year by the MaPHA Board, basically to address the poor immunisation and antenatal health indicators.

He also extended the management's appreciation to Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa and the Madang Provincial Government plus all other donors, partners, and stakeholders for their ongoing support to Madang PHA.

Meanwhile, a minute silence was also accorded yesterday at the beginning of the program as a sign of respect for the Late Sr. Karen Demok, who passed on early this week.

The Late Sr. Demok was a long- serving senior nursing officer at the Madang Provincial Hospital.

item.title: Usino/Bundi district gets new finance manager
item.description: The Usino/ Bundi District Development Authority has welcomed Helen Kavo as the district's new finance manager. The change brings to the end two decades of service by outgoing DFM Samuel Abel.
item.content:encoded:
The Usino/ Bundi District Development Authority has welcomed Helen Kavo as the district's new finance manager.

The change brings to the end two decades of service by outgoing DFM Samuel Abel.

The ceremony, held at the district office in Walium, saw Mr Abel formally hand over the responsibilities to his successor, Helen Kavo, who brings more than 30 years of professional experience in the finance sector.

The transition was witnessed by Deputy Secretary of the Department of Finance's Sub-national Division, Gabi Kila, who travelled from Port Moresby, District Administrator and Chief Executive Officer Johnson Wai, district management, finance and administration officers, Local Level Government representatives and other invited stakeholders.

In his farewell remarks, Mr Abel acknowledged that his time in the district finance office had been strengthened by teamwork, professional relationships, and the collective commitment of officers and stakeholders towards advancing the district's development aspirations.

Welcoming his successor, he wished Ms Kavo well as she takes responsibility for leading the Finance Division, expressing confidence in her ability to continue the work of strengthening the district's financial administration.

Incoming District Finance Manager, Ms Kavo expressed gratitude to the Department of Finance, PNG Treasury, the District Administration, and all stakeholders who contributed to a smooth transition.

Transferred from Port Moresby, Ms Kavo brings more than 30 years of professional experience in the finance sector to her new role.

Her appointment comes at an important time when effective financial management, accountabilit, and coordination are critical to supporting government-funded programmes and development activities throughout the district.

Meanwhile, the office of the local MP also acknowledged Mr Abel's valuable contributions and more than 20 years of dedicated service to the district.

The leadership transition highlights the importance of continuity in public administration, where individual responsibilities may change, but the obligation to manage public resources responsibly and serve communities remains constant.

As Usino Bundi Gama advances its development agenda, the District Administration and Finance Division will be expected to maintain close collaboration to ensure that public funds are managed in accordance with established financial regulations and that development priorities receive the necessary financial support.

item.title: Simbai youths lead community surrender program
item.description: Youths in the Simbai LLG area of the Middle Ramu district have taken a positive step towards restoring peace and good order by voluntarily surrendering their home-brewing bottles on Monday. They also participated in the uprooting of marijuana plants during the community surrender program at Simbai station.
item.content:encoded:
Youths in the Simbai LLG area of the Middle Ramu district have taken a positive step towards restoring peace and good order by voluntarily surrendering their home-brewing bottles on Monday.

They also participated in the uprooting of marijuana plants during the community surrender program at Simbai station.

The event was witnessed by police personnel from Madang Town, whose attendance at Simbai was facilitated through the support of Middle Ramu District Development Authority (MRDDA) under the chairmanship of local MP, Kansol Harwai Kamdaru.

The program also received support from Simbai LLG president, Nehemiah Kapa, and other local community leaders, who contributed to the community engagement and reconciliation efforts.

The initiative follows ongoing social problems, community tensions, and law and order challenges, including the burning of the temporary council chamber.

It also builds on a previous successful reconciliation between Simbai Central and Kaigen Zones, marking an important step towards rebuilding trust, forgiveness, and unity amongst the communities.

The program aims to encourage youths to take responsibility, discourage illegal activities, and strengthen cooperation between communities, police and government authorities across all four zones of Simbai LLG, including Simbai, Kaigen, Asai and Kairong.

The initiative represents a collective commitment to restoring peace, protecting public infrastructure, rebuilding community relationships, and creating a safer environment for government workers, service providers, and development partners.

The ultimate goal, however; is to restore Simbai's dignity, strengthen public confidence, and ensure that education and other government services, plus development opportunities, reach the people without fear or disruption.

This program marks a positive step towards a new beginning for Simbai, where peace, unity, respect for the law, and community responsibility become the foundation for lasting development.

Leaders in the area said homebrew, marijuana, sorcery, and unsettled land matters are major issues contributing to the detriment in law and order in Middle Ramu district.

item.title: Cancer care is significant milestone
item.description: Port Moresby General Hospital (PMGH) in collaboration with the Flowtint Group successfully completed the commissioning of its Computed Tomography (CT) Simulator, with international technical support over the past five days. The commissioning involved collaboration between international and local Medical Physicists, bringing together expertise from Australia, Sri Lanka and Papua New Guinea. As part
item.content:encoded:
Port Moresby General Hospital (PMGH) in collaboration with the Flowtint Group successfully completed the commissioning of its Computed Tomography (CT) Simulator, with international technical support over the past five days. The commissioning involved collaboration between international and local Medical Physicists, bringing together expertise from Australia, Sri Lanka and Papua New Guinea.

As part of the commissioning process, the Medical Physicists established baseline machine performance, conducted quality assurance measurements and verified that the CT Simulator met the required tolerance levels for optimal image quality. Importantly, the team characterized the relationship between CT Hounsfield Units (HU) and Relative Electron Density (RED) across different tissue-equivalent materials. These values were later incorporated into the Treatment Planning System (TPS) to facilitate accurate radiation dose calculations for radiotherapy treatment planning.

In a statement, P-M-G-H Chief Executive Officer Dr. Paki Molumi said the commissioning results will undergo final technical verification before submission to PMGH Clinical Governance for approval and subsequent release for clinical use.

This achievement represents another significant milestone in strengthening PMGH's capacity to deliver safe, accurate and quality-assured cancer treatment services in Papua New Guinea.
